lrw.text: Rhys is demoted as commander of the Hemlock pack after a failed ambush on a boggart party, and Gryffid takes over the pack.

Nath orders an attack on the Feast of Footbottom despite Rhys's report that it is a peaceful festival, and overwhelmed by feral boggarts Rhys invokes Colfenor's magic, causing a poison blast that kills everyone except himself, Gryffid and Nath and destroys his horns.
Nath and Gryffid brand him kin-slayer, traitor and outlaw, and they ambush him in Kinsbaile during the Festival of Tales, where Rhys kills Nath and the elves leave, sparing the kithkin.
After the Great Aurora turns the plane into Shadowmoor, a coalition including Maralen and Rhys defeats Oona, and Maralen becomes queen of the fae and binds Rhys to her, granting him immortality.

mor.text: Rhys, blamed for a cataclysmic event that killed many elves and with his horns broken, is hunted by his own society.
Ashling, Brigid and the Vendilion clique find him with a message from Colfenor, who names him his final pupil and asks him to plant his seed cone in the Murmuring Bosk.

Rhys finds the Bosk destroyed and plants the seedcone with an ancient blessing, then Nath and Gryffid ambush the party at Kinsbaile and Nath challenges him to a duel, which Rhys wins by twisting Nath's head by the horns until his neck snaps.
Colfenor burns to death as planned, and a young treefolk rises at the Bosk a day later.

shm.text: Colfenor takes Rhys as his apprentice and teaches him yew magic, and later sends him from Kinsbaile to plant his seed cone at the Murmuring Bosk, which Rhys, Ashling and Brigid find leveled and burned.
Trapped by his former tribesmen, Rhys fights and kills Taercenn Nath, breaking the siege of Kinsbaile, and Gryffid finds Nath's body and swears to kill him.
Ashling is rekindled and her fire engulfs Colfenor, who dies as the last yew despite Rhys's efforts, and his sapling rises one day later.
Oona is finally defeated at Glen Elendra with the sacrifice of the Sapling of Colfenor, and Maralen becomes queen of the fae as day returns.

eve.text: Oona is defeated by Maralen, Rhys, Brigid, Sygg, Ashling and Colfenor's sapling, though her consciousness survives, and Maralen gives Rhys a moonglove flower to use on her if Oona returns through her, which leaves him unable to die until then.
Oko manipulates Rhys into believing Maralen is becoming Oona, and Rhys strikes her with moonglove, keeping the promise, until Oko admits he roused Isilu and turned Rhys against her.
Oko cures Maralen with dawnglow and Eirdu appears to offset Isilu, so Rhys is at peace, and he declines a new oath, bids Maralen farewell, and fades into a shower of petals.

ecl.text: Maralen becomes queen of the fae and binds herself to Rhys with a death pact, and Rhys visits her and is reminded that he would kill her if she followed Oona's path.
Believing his promise demands it, Rhys approaches Maralen with a poisoned dagger, calling her Oona, and cuts her arm, and she bleeds petals and collapses, stunning him that she did not fight back.
Oko tells Rhys that Maralen is not Oona reborn and spares him since Rhys thought he was destroying a tyrant, and he drips dawnglow into Maralen's mouth.
Maralen forgives Rhys but realizes his old promise is gone, and he thanks Eirdu and Maralen and dissolves into flower petals.
